done_when: The shared test lane admits one test run per four available cores, at least one (two on an 8-core machine), each test command still getting half the machine's cores as its worker count; forge doctor, the lanes view and the pane show the test lane's size; the coordinator guide says so; command tests cover an 8-core machine admitting two test runs while a third waits, and a 4-core machine keeping one, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: The previous P2 remains open. With two running tests, the expanded counts occupy 37 columns. After 100 seconds, an active Tests stage and total time add 28 columns. In the compact renderer, pane.ts:137–143 reserves both boxes with flexShrink: 0, requiring 65 columns in a 60-column prompt and clipping timing on terminal and desktop surfaces. The command-backed test concatenates node text without checking allocated widths; native compact checks cover 79 columns. Budget counts and timing together so their reserved widths fit the prompt.
findings.title: Keep expanded compact counts within the prompt width

why: The machine-wide test lane runs one test run at a time, so on an 8-core machine three or more closes and worker test runs often queue behind each other while cores sit idle (owner, 2026-10-09: two test runs at once, each with half the cores)
